title: Effect of two different weight-loss rates on body composition and strength and power-related performance in elite athletes (Garthe et al. 2011)
content: Garthe I et al., 2011 — Compared a slower (~0.7% body weight/week) vs. a faster (~1.4% body weight/week) rate of weight loss in elite athletes. The slower-loss group showed more favorable body-composition and strength/power outcomes in this study's context. Applicability is explicitly to elite/trained athletes in a competition-prep-like context — this finding should NOT be generalized as a mandatory rule for every user regardless of training status or goal.

title: Effect of two different weight-loss rates on body composition and strength and power-related performance in elite athletes (Garthe et al. 2011)
content: Garthe et al. 2011 — Product implication: a gradual, slower rate of weight loss CAN be preferable when preserving lean mass/performance matters to the user's goal — this can inform a general reference range for pace of loss, but must be applied as a personalized, non-mandatory guideline (PRODUCT_HEURISTIC informed by athlete-specific evidence), not a universal law copied onto every user regardless of training background, medical status, or stated preference.
